question: By selling 6 articles for a rupee, a man loses 30%. To gain 40% how many must he sell for a rupee?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a fixed amount, the quantity sold is inversely proportional to the selling price percentage.

Formula: Q₁ × SP₁% = Q₂ × SP₂%

⇒ 6 × (100 − 30) = Q₂ × (100 + 40)

⇒ 6 × 70 = Q₂ × 140

⇒ 420 = 140 × Q₂ ⇒ Q₂ = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3 articles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 SP₁ = 70%

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP₁) of 6 articles = ₹1

⇒ SP₁ per article = ₹ 1/6

Loss percentage = 30%

⇒ SP₁ = (100 − 30)% of CP = 70% of CP

⇒ 70% of CP = 1/6

⇒ CP = (1/6) × (100/70) = ₹ 5/21

**To find SP for 40% gain:**

⇒ New SP (SP₂) = (100 + 40)% of CP = 140% of CP

⇒ SP₂ = 140% × (5/21)

⇒ SP₂ = (140/100) × (5/21) = (7/5) × (5/21) = ₹ 1/3

Since the new selling price is ₹ 1/3 per article,

⇒ Number of articles to be sold for ₹1 = 1 ÷ (1/3) = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3 articles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price and Quantity Relationship

When the total expenditure or selling amount remains constant, the price per item is inversely proportional to the quantity of items (Price × Quantity = Constant).

Basic Profit and Loss Rules

Profit occurs when SP > CP (Profit = SP − CP) and Loss occurs when CP > SP (Loss = CP − SP). Both profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Selling Price Formula

SP can be directly found from CP using the multiplier: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 or SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.
